sentences.text: It is essentially on account of the fact that money value does not remain constant over a long spell of years and thus claimant being aged only 40 years, he has long years ahead of him to look forward to, the sliding value of the money will have adverse impact on his future prospects.

Accordingly, having due regard to the fact that he was aged about 40 years at the time of the accident, 25% of his established income will have to be factored in towards compensation for 'loss of future prospects'.

Therefore, 'loss of earning capacity' is recomputed as follows:
Rs.6,000/- + 25% (Rs.1,500/-) =Rs.7,500/- Rs.7,500/- X 12 X 15 X 20% =

This is also similar case and learned counsel for insurance company fairly concedes to it.
Accordingly, loss of future prospects deserves to be added and given age of the petitioner 40% of established income will have to be given towards compensation for loss of future prospects.

Therefore, 'loss of earning capacity' is computed as follows:
- 12 - Rs.9,500/- + 40% = Rs.13,300/- X 12 X 17 X 25% = Rs.6,78,000/- as against Rs.5,10,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
13.
Given the nature of injuries, laid up period has to be considered as six months and the petitioner would be entitled to a sum of Rs.57,000/- (Rs.9,500/- X 6) under the said head.
Towards 'medical expenses' based on the actual bills submitted, a sum of Rs.2,02,700/- is awarded.
I deem the same to be appropriate.
Towards 'miscellaneous expenses' a sum of Rs.7,300/- is awarded.
I deem the same to be appropriate.
Towards 'attendant charges' a sum of Rs.40,000/- is awarded.
I deem the same to be appropriate.
Towards future medical expenses, a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded, I deem it appropriate.
Towards 'pain and sufferings' a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- is awarded.
Petitioner has suffered in total seven fractures and under the circumstances I deem it appropriate to reduce it to Rs.1,40,000/-.

Thus, petitioner is entitled to total a - 13 - compensation of Rs.11,45,300/- as against Rs.10,40,000/- awarded by the Tribunal along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization.

sentences.text: [2014 1 SCC 244] has considered annual income of 10 year old boy at Rs.30,000/- and the age of the younger parent was considered for multiplier.

As per the said decision, in the instant case notional income of the deceased has to be considered at Rs.30,000/- annually and the age of the parent being 27 years, a multiplier of 17 is applicable and accordingly 'loss of dependency' is calculated as: Rs.30,000/- X 17 = Rs.5,10,000/-.

Further, under conventional heads, a sum of Rs.30,000/- is awarded towards 'loss of estate and funeral expenses' and further a sum of Rs.40,000/- each is awarded in favour of both the petitioners, totaling to Rs.80,000/-.
Thus, petitioners are entitled to a compensation of - 15 - Rs.6,20,000/- (Rs.5,10,000/- + 30,000/- + 80,000/-) as against Rs.3,00,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Respondent No.2-insurance company is liable to pay the said amount to the petitioners along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization.

MFA No.3084/2019 is allowed in part and it is held that respondent No.2-insurance company is liable to pay the petitioners a sum of Rs.6,20,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition before Tribunal till realization within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
